items.title: WiseLSTM: a depthwise CNN--LSTM framework with metaheuristic optimization for offshore wind power forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: Reliable one-hour-ahead wind-power forecasting can support scheduling andenergy-management decisions in renewable-to-hydrogen systems. … These results highlight the joint importance of efficient localfeature extraction, recurrent temporal modeling, and configuration stability foroffshore wind-power forecasting.

items.title: PEAKSAFE-AI: Explainable Multi-Agent Peak-Demand Forecasting with Uncertainty-Aware Assurance and Human-in-the-Loop Decision Support
items.summary: From the abstract: This study develops PEAKSAFE-AI, an explainable three-agent decision-support prototype integrating XGBoost forecasting, TreeSHAP evidence attribution, and validation-calibrated interval-based assurance. … PEAKSAFE-AI demonstrates a transparent forecast-to-escalation workflow, while remaining an offline prototype rather than a live grid-control system.

items.title: A TCN-Transformer Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Multi-source Feature Fusion
items.summary: From the abstract: To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-branch parallel TCN-Transformer hybrid deep learning model for daily multivariate time series forecasting. … Taking daily inbound passenger flow of the Hong Kong-Macau Ferry Terminal as an empirical case, experiments on a three-year dataset show that the proposed model achieves an R² of 0.953, an RMSE of 357.93 and an MAE of 274.27 on the test set, outperforming single TCN, Transformer, LSTM and CNN baselines.

items.title: Fair Walk-Forward Forecasting of ICE Robusta Futures: Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, Deep-Learning, and Hybrid Models
items.summary: From the abstract: This study empirically compares 14 statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA)–recurrent hybrid specifications for the daily ICE Futures Europe Robusta Coffee benchmark, rather than proposing a new forecasting algorithm. … Delta-Random Forest achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) at 83.59 USD per metric ton, whereas Khashei–Bijari ARIMA–Long Short‐Term Memory (LSTM) yields the lowest root mean squared error at 111.99.

items.title: From data-driven differential equations to mechanistic forecasting with machine learning
items.summary: From the abstract: We then transform this framework into a forecasting model by predicting the time-varying parameters and substituting these predictions into the learned equations. … By dynamically adapting to temporal shifts, our proposed model achieved a mean absolute error below 3% for learning a time series and below 6% for forecasting up to a month ahead.

items.title: From Fixed Defaults to Calibrated Activation Policies for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We develop a calibrated selection policy that learns a reliable default from prior experiments, adapts the activation function and its location to each task, and retains the default when evidence for a change is insufficient. … In an evaluation supported by 1,225 Informer training runs across 17 dataset variants and 51 forecasting tasks, the policy reduces mean squared error by 7.86% on average relative to the conventional fixed-activation baseline and improves 72.55% of tasks.

items.title: Learning From Static Context in Federated Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We ask whether a federated TFT can learn from it. … Per-batch FedAdam, which aggregates gradients after every batch, uses the static input almost as well as central training, whereas communication-efficient schemes with local epochs (FedAvg, FedAdam+Prox) extract far less from it and gain nothing significant on either application dataset.

items.title: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: From the abstract: Time series forecasting is critical for demand prediction and resource management in modern Web services, yet applying pretrained Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) to downstream tasks remains challenging due to domain shifts. … To address this problem, we argue that temporal patterns should be reused at a decomposition level, as effective trend and seasonal dynamics may originate from different contexts.

items.title: Short-Term Load Forecasting for a Campus Building: Regression with Residual Correction and Gaussian Smoothing versus a Feedforward Neural Network
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper compares two hourly forecasting approaches for Shepard Hall at The City College of New York using metered load data from 2022 to January 2026. … The results show that a simple, interpretable regression with targeted post-processing can outperform a deeper neural network for single-building forecasting with limited data.

items.title: Evaluation of Deep Learning Models for Time Series Forecasting in Financial Markets
items.summary: From the abstract: This research examines the application of long-term short-term memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in forecasting stock price by taking advantage of historical market data. … This study compares the effectiveness of these models in predicting stock price movements, using key matrix such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), R-squared (R²) and accuracy.

items.title: Solar-Irradiance Forecasting in Arid Climates: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Models and Probabilistic-Uncertainty Quantification Using Four Years of Riyadh Data
items.summary: From the abstract: Precise short-horizon solar-irradiance forecasting is essential for grid-tied inverter control and battery scheduling in arid climates, yet model performance in regions with frequent dust remains under-characterized. … This study benchmarks six machine-learning models—Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)—for 1-, 3-, and 6-h-ahead Global Horizontal Irradiance forecasting using 34,871 hourly records from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (2013–2016).

items.title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose CATF, a Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting framework built on a Manager-Worker architecture: a Transformer-based Manager routes each input to a single Worker based on the context, using hard routing during both training and inference. … On five context-rich datasets, four horizons, and two normalization schemes, CATF improves over its standalone counterpart in 162 of 200 comparisons, the best CATF-enhanced model outperforms the best standalone baseline in 19 of 20 settings, and it outperforms the zero-shot Time-MoE foundation model in 15 of 20 settings.

items.title: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce the Koopman Generative Operator (KGO), a probabilistic forecasting method that conceptualizes prediction as the evolution of structured uncertainty. … By unifying these components, KGO achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on 13/17 ProbTS benchmarks in CRPS and 16/17 in NMAE.

items.title: OmniST: Topology-Invariant Spatiotemporal Forecasting with Guaranteed-Coverage Uncertainty at Unseen Sensor Locations
items.summary: From the abstract: We present OmniST, a topology-invariant forecaster whose computation has zero structural dependency on the number of nodes, and which, composed with inductive split-conformal calibration, gives distribution-free, coverage-guaranteed prediction intervals at arbitrary (including never-seen) sensor locations, preserving that guarantee as sensors are added or removed. … On real Delhi air-quality data (37 stations, 2019-2023), OmniST attains a 30-day PM2.5 MAE of 31.0 ug/m3 and degrades at most 1.1 percent when 40 percent of stations are removed.

items.title: GlucoAgent: Personalized Glucose Forecasting from Multimodal Personal Context
items.summary: From the abstract: We present GlucoAgent, an LLM-based agentic system that addresses this challenge through dynamic, case-by-case analysis at inference time. … On CGMacros, a multimodal glucose dataset, GlucoAgent outperforms time series foundation models on every forecasting horizon, achieving an average RMSE of 22.5 mg/dL compared to 23.5 mg/dL of Chronos-2, the leading multimodal time series foundation model.

items.title: The influence of ensemble size and composition on the performance of combined real-time COVID-19 forecasts
items.summary: From the abstract: Using data from the European COVID-19 Forecast Hub we investigated these questions, with the aim of offering practical guidance to organisers of multi-model prediction platforms during infectious disease outbreaks. … We found that including more models both improved and stabilised aggregate ensemble performance, while selecting for better component models did not yield any particular advantage.

items.title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates
items.summary: From the abstract: Building on this, we propose Context as Covariates (CoCo), a forecasting framework in which an LLM distills its textual reasoning into numerically grounded forecast and confidence covariates that guide a TSFM backbone, thereby exploiting the strengths of both LLMs and TSFMs. … Notably, CoCo with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the LLM and Chronos2 as the TSFM achieves up to 12% MAE improvement over state-of-the-art TSFMs and LLM forecasters, such as GPT-4o.

items.title: The leakage premium in decomposition-based cryptocurrency forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: Decomposition-ensemble models, which split a price series into components with methods such as CEEMDAN and VMD and forecast each component with a neural network, report remarkable accuracy for cryptocurrency returns. This paper shows that most of that accuracy is look-ahead.

items.title: Utility-Gated Personalized Federated Forecasting for Peak-Constrained Building Energy Management
items.summary: From the abstract: This study examines whether selective, communication-efficient collaboration improves both load prediction and battery operation. … At the 96-step horizon, the method reduces Solar-Energy mean squared error by 1.59% relative to local training and avoids the greater than 3% degradation caused by unconditional federation on Electricity, using half the communication of federated averaging.

items.title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Oil and Gas Data Forecasting and Well Event Detection
items.summary: From the abstract: This study evaluates the efficacy of a newly developed time series foundation model against existing state-of-the-art foundation models for forecasting operational sensor dynamics across diverse well event regimes. … However, the evaluation also highlights specific limitations; the proposed model is less effective under conditions where operational changes are sudden and abrupt, scenarios in which alternative models exhibit lower error rates.

items.title: Regime-Aware Data Cleaning for Production Forecasting in Unconventional Wells: A Change Point Segmentation, Data Cleaning, and Conformal Prediction Workflow
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper introduces a regime aware workflow that changes the order in which production data are interpreted: the history is first partitioned into interpretable producing regimes, outlier detection is then applied locally within each regime, point forecast models are trained on the locally cleaned data, and conformal prediction intervals are calibrated on regime relevant residuals. … The workflow was evaluated on 521 daily reported Montney gas wells (northeastern British Columbia, Canada; July 2017–January 2025).

items.title: An Integrated Machine Learning and Time-Series Forecasting Framework for Predicting Hydrate Blockage Dynamics in Pipelines
items.summary: From the abstract: This work presents a physics-guided hybrid machine learning and multivariate time-series forecasting framework for predicting pressure-drop evolution, hydrate progression, and blockage proximity using real field-trial data. … These outputs, together with operating-condition features and pressure history, are incorporated into a conditional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to forecast future pressure-drop evolution and blockage timing.

items.title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: From the abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood. … Using this framework, we conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation of popular TSFMs across diverse datasets and show that current models exhibit distinct and systematic patterns of miscalibration that standard metrics often obscure.

items.title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
items.summary: From the abstract: We compare three zero-shot time-series foundation models (Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M and Chronos-2, 8192-hour context, no covariates) with the Khepri v1.5 SARIMA and GBM baselines, with their code and hyperparameters unchanged, for 96-hour forecasts of hourly carbon intensity in the Nordic bidding zones NO1-NO5 and SE1-SE4. … On the 2025 test (361 daily origins, contamination not ruled out) all three models have a lower zone-averaged MAPE than both baselines, by 0.952 to 1.347 percentage points (Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction, all p < 0.0001), and each beats SARIMA in 9 of 9 zones.

items.title: SynForecast: Controlled Synthetic Time Series for Forecasting Research
items.summary: From the abstract: We present SynForecast, an open-source Python library with 32 generators, 19 of which implement named mechanisms with a published source in econometrics, quantitative finance, statistical physics and point-process theory. … A synthetic prior outperforms the same network trained from scratch at a fixed budget by up to 34% with a few dozen observations, but loses to it at full history at every frequency, and none of three pre-specified rescalings of history predicts where the sign changes.

items.title: Investigating the effects of the patch size in Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: From the abstract: We study how this choice interacts with transformer architecture through a controlled comparison of encoder-only and decoder-only forecasting models trained with the same data mixture and optimization budget. … Across 97 GIFT-Eval tasks, encoder-only models consistently benefit from smaller patches, whereas decoder-only performance follows a U-shaped trend, with an intermediate patch size performing best in aggregate.

items.title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction
items.summary: From the abstract: Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. … Under one shared evaluation pipeline, the 60-minute MAE of ST-GFM is 3.5% below a retrained STAEformer on METR-LA and 13.0% below it on PEMS-BAY.

items.title: Forecast Combination with Temporal Validation and Context Memory
items.summary: From the abstract: We study a fixed context-weighted rule and two variants that select their parameters using completed historical target blocks. … ValidationMix has mean series MASE 0.2855 versus 0.3109 for RecencyMean on M4 Weekly, and 0.8993 versus 0.9085 on M3 Monthly.

items.title: Prequential Evaluation of Adaptive Prediction Intervals: A Fifteen-Series Replay Study
items.summary: From the abstract: Adaptive prediction intervals can have accurate average coverage while retaining substantial local coverage error. … At nominal 80% coverage, their mean rolling absolute coverage errors are 0.0656 and 0.0645, compared with 0.0830 for unadjusted intervals.

items.title: Code and results: When Do Time Series Foundation Models Help Forecast Wind Energy Droughts? A Preregistered Evaluation
items.summary: From the abstract: The study evaluates time series foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Moirai-2) against climatology, model output statistics, quantile regression and a recurrent network for probabilistic forecasts of the cumulative wind energy deficit in 16 regions in Europe, Australia and the US. … The protocol was registered on OSF (https://osf.io/ph7nr/) before the prespecified main analysis of the sealed test period (January 2024 to September 2026) was scored once.

items.title: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We address both questions for a six-qubit gate-based reservoir that forecasts next-day motor-insurance claim counts. … Small QRC models can thus reach competitive accuracy on this task, and hardware-aware layout selection makes their transfer to IBM Kingston more consistent.

items.title: RateIN: Time Series Foundation Models Have a Sampling Problem
items.summary: From the abstract: We present RateIN, an inference-time wrapper that resamples the context by a factor k, lets a frozen model forecast on the new grid, and brings the quantile forecast back to the native grid. … On GIFT-Eval, RateIN lowers the CRPS of all six models we tested, from 1.4M to 256M parameters, by 0.5 to 11 % against the same model with a sign-flip augmentation (the average of its forecasts for x and −x).

items.title: HQNN-CL: Regime-Aware Hybrid Quantum Neural Network with Continual Learning for Financial Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To achieve uncertainty-aware robust financial forecasting in the face of changing market conditions, this study proposes a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Continual Learning (HQNN-CL). … The experimental results show that HQNN-CL has outperformed other methods on the Systems Limited (RMSE = 3.0149) and Teradata (RMSE = 0.8909) datasets and is within 0.32% and 0.40% of the best baseline method for Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services, respectively.

items.title: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling
items.summary: From the abstract: In this work, we develop a Transformer-based architecture for simultaneous forecasting and temporal downscaling. … Our approach provides a scalable and efficient framework for multi-resolution solar irradiance forecasting and temporal downscaling, suitable for practical energy forecasting and grid management applications.

items.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Task-Free Federated Continual Forecasting via Two-Tier Replay under Concept Drift
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in task-free federated forecasting under concept drift. … Experiments on the Beijing Multi-Site Air- Quality dataset with 12 clients, three forecasting targets, and three horizons show that TwoTierReplay achieves the best stability-plasticity score in all nine target-horizon configurations.

items.title: Forecasting Visitor Demand from Open AI-Camera Counts and Weather: Lessons from Japan for Saudi Heritage Sites
items.summary: From the abstract: Using 22 months of open AI-camera counts from three contrasting sites in Fukui, Japan (a train station, a coastal cliff and a mountain summit park), we measure how weather changes visits, forecast daily counts up to a week ahead with only the weather forecast available at the time, test busy-day warnings tied to a staffing decision, and ask how much history a new counter needs. … With the forecasts actually issued, three-day-ahead weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) at the summit park falls from 38.5% to 31.9% (Diebold-Mariano p<0.001), and the gain holds to five days; the sheltered station gains nothing.

items.title: ContextGuard: Reliability-gated repair for frozen time-series foundation models under sensor dropout
items.summary: From the abstract: ContextGuard recovers failed sensor channels from their synchronized peers before an unchanged probabilistic forecaster is called. … It estimates regularized cross-channel structure on an early training segment, calibrates a bounded per-channel weight on a later segment, and activates recovery only when the calibrated improvement over the pooled-mean fallback exceeds a fixed threshold.

items.title: Knowledge-Guided Probabilistic Forecasting of Urban Land-Surface Temperature in Three Moroccan Cities
items.summary: From the abstract: The contribution is therefore a reproducible accuracy–physical-consistency trade-off within a probabilistic forecasting pipeline rather than a claim of predictive or uncertainty superiority.

items.title: Dynamic modelling and forecasting of interest rates: evidence from Scandinavian countries
items.summary: From the abstract: Using unique data of three Scandinavian countries (Denmark, Norway and Sweden), the study examines the term structure of their interest rates and the performance of the Babbs and Nowman model in forecasting the rates covering their economic stability and financial crisis periods from 2000 to 2014. … The findings further exhibit that when considering the forecasting errors, the continuous-time models generate superior forecasts, a feature of great interest in pricing interest rate derivatives and hedging strategies.

items.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the interactions between multivariate time series and heterogeneous covariates, which commonly arise in scientific applications. … Across various benchmarks, Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on average by improving skill scores by 5.2 percentage points relative to the strongest baselines and increasing win rates by 10 percentage points.

items.title: QUAL: Quantile Alignment Improves Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: From the abstract: Motivated by this finding, we propose QUAL (Quantile alignment), a simple label-free framework for improving and combining diverse TSFMs. … On GIFT-Eval, quantile alignment reduces average member MASE and CRPS by 7.4% and 9.8%.

items.title: PCD: Predictive Coding Dynamics for Irregularly Sampled Time Series
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose Predictive Coding Dynamics (PCD), a residual feedback mechanism for irregular continuous dynamic models. … Experiments on forecasting and trajectory recovery tasks show that PCD improves continuous dynamic backbones under sparse and irregular sampling.

items.title: SensorFault-Bench
items.summary: From the abstract: SensorFault-Bench evaluates forecasting architectures and robustness-improvement methods for cyber-physical systems under controlled sensor faults on real input histories. … It reports worst-scenario degradation, clean mean squared error, and worst-scenario fault-time mean squared error.

items.title: Comparison of Machine Learning Methods for Monthly Rainfall Forecasting Using k-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, and Artificial Neural Networks
items.summary: From the abstract: Rainfall is an important meteorological parameter across various sectors and exhibits complex nonlinear characteristics, requiring reliable forecasting methods. This study aims to compare the performance of three machine learning algorithms—k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), Random Forest (RF), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN)—for monthly rainfall forecasting at the Depati Amir Meteorological Station, Pangkalpinang, using data from 2015 to 2024.

items.title: STG-Mixer: A Multi-Region, Multi-Step Forecasting Network for Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease with Multi-Timescale Feature Extraction and Spatial Association Learning
items.summary: From the abstract: Accurate forecasting of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) incidence is crucial for effective prevention and control. … In this study, we propose Spatiotemporal Graph Mixer (STG-Mixer), a multi-region, multi-step forecasting network for HFMD based on multi-timescale feature extraction and spatial association learning.

items.title: IMRouter: Imbalance-aware Temporal Pattern Routing for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To address this issue, we propose IMRouter (Imbalance-aware Temporal Pattern Routing), a novel framework that mitigates TPI-induced biases in both temporal representation learning and cross-modal alignment. … Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of IMRouter, particularly in improving forecasting performance on less frequent temporal patterns.

items.title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: This work develops a physics-informed multimodal deep learning framework for 10- to 110-minute-ahead probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasting. … The proposed model outperforms all 14 baselines, achieving a forecast skill score (FSS) of 0.2950, 0.099 above the next-best model.

items.title: FARE: Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion for Retail Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose FARE(Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion), which ranks historical weeks separately for each known target-week factor and merges the selected weeks into a factor reference under a fixed budget. … On Favorita, M5, Rossmann, and Rohlik, FARE reduces the weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) of five backbones by 11.46%, 4.06%, 14.63%, and 10.16% on average.

items.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Quantile Demand Forecasting in E-commerce with Doubly Censored Data
items.summary: From the abstract: In this paper, we introduce a straightforward framework for learning quantiles from doubly-censored observations and propose a tailored evaluation metric. … Finally, inventory simulations and real-world applications confirm the practical utility of our method in retail operations.

items.title: Understanding axial attention in TSFMs through single location regression
items.summary: From the abstract: Recent advances in Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) increasingly rely on axial attention mechanisms, but despite their empirical success, the theoretical properties of axial attention remain largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we extend the Single Location Regression framework introduced in Marion et al. [2025] to 2D structured data, in order to study sparse information settings where a target depends on a small number of tokens.

items.title: Multistep and Multivariate Time Series Explainability with GradientSHAP: A Wind Power Case Study
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper introduces a carefully adapted GradientSHAP approach to provide interpretability for multivariate, multistep wind power forecasting -- a largely underexplored area.

items.title: Big Data Applications and Intelligent Decision Support Framework for Study Tourism Market Demand Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper addresses three critical bottlenecks in study tourism market demand forecasting: data heterogeneity, time series non-stationarity, and decision-making lag, proposing a big data-driven intelligent decision support framework termed BDIDS (Big Data Intelligent Decision Support). … The predictive layer introduces a cross-modal attention fusion mechanism, coordinating BERT semantic embeddings with time series statistical features to drive an improved Transformer-LSTM hybrid model.

items.title: Variance reduction and interval efficiency in forecast reconciliation
items.summary: From the abstract: Forecast reconciliation is commonly motivated by variance reduction, whereas finite-sample interval widths depend on order statistics. … We also compare existing covariance estimators on two related Australian retail partitions and a tourism hierarchy.

items.title: Turning time series into algebraic equations: Symbolic machine learning for interpretable modeling of chaotic time series
items.summary: From the abstract: To address this gap, we propose two complementary symbolic forecasters that learn explicit, interpretable algebraic equations from chaotic time series data. … Across datasets, symbolic forecasters achieve competitive one-step-ahead accuracy while providing transparent analytical equations that reveal salient aspects of the underlying dynamics.

items.title: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research
items.summary: From the abstract: To address these challenges, we propose TSFLab, a self-improving agent-agnostic "workbench" that equips compatible coding agents with shared resources and tools for low-cost TSF research and continuous maintenance of research resources. … In reproduction and benchmarking, TSFLab improves task completion by 20-163% and cuts fresh tokens per completed task by 11-66% across baselines.

items.title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We develop two hybrid forecasting architectures that integrate the ADR physical PV efficiency model with the TSMixer neural forecasting architecture through feature augmentation and residual learning. … These findings suggest that, for modern deep forecasting architectures trained on large datasets, explicitly incorporating the ADR physical model provides limited practical benefit for day-ahead PV forecasting.

items.title: Modular Bayesian Foundation Models: Bayesian time series encoders for OOD detection, routing and forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose a modular foundation model framework that combines end-to-end Bayesian encoder training with uncertainty based routing. … We evaluate this framework on time-series data through distribution shift, encoder selection, and probabilistic forecasting.

items.title: REVBRAIN: Real-time Probabilistic EEG Forecasting Using Residual Vector Quantization
items.summary: From the abstract: In this paper, we present REVBRAIN, a probabilistic deep learning method that produces forecasts in real time by generating the forecast over the whole prediction horizon at once. This is achieved by tokenizing the output space using residual vector quantization (RVQ) and generating forecasts over the items in the tokenized space.

items.title: RainCheck: Harnessing Historical Weather Data with Machine Learning for Rainfall Forecasting in Bangladesh
items.summary: From the abstract: Machine-learning rainfall forecasts are often evaluated by shuffling station records into random training and test sets. … We release a leakage-aware protocol and code so that future station-based studies report skill against climatology on held-out years.

items.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce FACTS-MAS, a domain-agnostic multi-agent forecasting framework that decomposes evidence into specialized channels for temporal dynamics, exogenous context, seasonality, structural information, and discrete events. … Our method outperforms both a naive last-value forecast method and the TimesFM foundation model.

items.title: Timestral
items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce Timestral, a family of four time series foundation models for probabilistic forecasting, with 5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M parameters. Timestral sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, where Timestral-209M and Timestral-123M take the top two places on every metric.

items.title: RankFormer: Rethinking Time Series Transformers through Representation Capacity Analysis and Progressive Decoding
items.summary: From the abstract: To address these challenges, we propose RankFormer, a novel encoder-decoder architecture for multivariate time series forecasting. We establish a rank-based analysis framework to investigate how tokenization, embedding, and attention designs affect the representation capacity of time series Transformers.

items.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To combine graph-aware traffic modeling with zero-shot adaptation, we introduce the Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Network (GAS-PFN). … Across six benchmarks at the 90-minute horizon, GAS-PFN reduces MSE by 34.0% on average relative to TimePFN, its closest PFN-based predecessor.

items.title: Pneuma: A Large-Scale Real-World Time Series Benchmark for Commercial Aircraft Predictive Maintenance
items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce Pneuma, the first publicly available large-scale benchmark for predictive maintenance using onboard time series from in-service commercial aircraft. … We structure the benchmark around three tasks: multivariate forecasting, supervised fault classification, and unsupervised anomaly detection, with labels derived from actual maintenance records.

items.title: Learning from Points and Patches: A Pre-trained Hybrid Attention Transformer for Time Series Analysis
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose TimeHAT (Hybrid Attention Transformer), a general-purpose pre-training framework for time-series analysis that addresses two complementary questions: what to learn and how to learn. … We evaluate TimeHAT across real-world datasets and four downstream tasks: classification, long-term forecasting, imputation, and anomaly detection.

items.title: RAG-CSI: Global Local Retrieval via Joint State and Dynamics Matching for CSI Prediction
items.summary: From the abstract: Channel state information (CSI) prediction forecasts future channel states from historical observations, supporting transceiver design and resource allocation with reduced measurement overhead. … In this paper, we propose RAG-CSI, a retrieval-enhanced Transformer framework that augments prediction with relevant historical channel knowledge.

items.title: Decomposition-Based Preprocessing Versus Architectural Complexity in Neural Forecasting of Economic and Financial Time Series: A Comparative Empirical Study
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper examines under what conditions input preprocessing through mathematical signal decomposition can substitute for architectural complexity in neural models applied to nonstationary economic and financial series. … The results show that variational mode decomposition consistently provides the largest accuracy gains across all three architectures and reduces by up to one order of magnitude the number of neurons required by recurrent models to achieve competitive performance.

items.title: ARIMA-Based Forecasting of Air Pollutant Concentrations in North Cyprus: A Multi-Station, Multi-Pollutant Time Series Study
items.summary: From the abstract: Air pollution monitoring and forecasting in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) remains critically understudied. … Three model types — Simple Seasonal, Winters’ Additive, and exponential smoothing with ARIMA extension — were tailored to station-and pollutant-specific characteristics.

items.title: CADENCE: Distributional Next-Transaction Forecasting for Business Cash-Flow Underwriting
items.summary: From the abstract: We present CADENCE, Calendar-Aware Distributional Event Network for Cash-Flow Estimation, a compact causal Transformer that treats each transaction as a token and predicts the amount and a full, nonparametric timing distribution of every cash flow's next payment. … Against the production FFT baseline, CADENCE improves one-day timing accuracy by 93.3% and next-event F1 by 6.7%, while producing calibrated distributions that serve directly as a confidence gate for downstream decisions.

items.title: Self-Supervised Latent Action-Conditioned World Modeling for Time Series
items.summary: From the abstract: Building on this hypothesis, we propose ACTS-WM, a self-supervised latent action-conditioned world model framework for time-series analysis. … We evaluate ACTS-WM across 4 representative tasks on 22 datasets from diverse domains, covering univariate and multivariate forecasting and classification.

items.title: Selective Transfer Learning for Groundwater Level Anomaly Forecasting: Accuracy-Risk Trade-offs
items.summary: From the abstract: This work studies context-aware selective transfer learning for multi-well groundwater anomaly forecasting in the Netherlands. Source-domain pretraining can raise average accuracy but is not uniformly reliable: it degrades performance on a substantial fraction of heterogeneous wells.

items.title: SpecLST: Spectral-Enhanced Long-Short Term Spatio-Temporal Multimodal Modeling for Traffic Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To address these limitations, we propose SpecLST, a frequency-enhanced long-short-term spatio-temporal multimodal framework. SpecLST leverages a fast Fourier transform-based frequency-domain representation module to efficiently encode multi-week historical dependencies, bypassing the memory bottlenecks of standard attention mechanisms over raw long sequences.

items.title: STeP-TS: Shared Temporal Filters with Pruning for Time Series
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose a compact one-layer convolutional framework that learns a shared bank of multi-scale temporal filters of each variable.

items.title: TimeWorld: Towards Action-Conditioned Multimodal World Models for Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To investigate these gaps, we introduce TSWM-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for multimodal TSWMs spanning seven real-world datasets, with textual interventions grounded in recorded action--outcome data. Our evaluation reveals that conventional multimodal forecasters underperform history-only time series foundation models (TSFMs) despite dataset-specific training, whereas simple text-prefix adaptations improve forecasting across all evaluated TSFM backbones.

items.title: VRATF: Vision-based Retrieval-Augmented Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To address this limitation, this paper proposes VRATF, a vision-based retrieval-augmented time series forecasting framework. VRATF first extracts low-frequency trend components from historical sequences using frequency-domain filtering, renders the denoised trends as line-chart images, and encodes them with a frozen vision encoder to construct a visual retrieval database.

items.title: Encoding Time Series Dynamics with Sliding-Window Signatures for Online Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: In many applications, however, the time series of interest are non-stationary and the relationship between target and inputs evolves over time, requiring forecasters that adapt online. … For French national electricity load forecasting, our method outperforms various state-of-the-art approaches.

items.title: Dynamic Multi-Step Decoding for Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: From the abstract: We argue that the optimal decoding strategy is not fixed across inputs, but should be selected adaptively for each forecasting instance. We propose a dynamic strategy selector that treats the forecast rollout schedule as an inference-time decision problem for frozen pretrained time-series foundation models.

items.title: MetaARIMA: Configuration-Level Transfer Learning for ARIMA Models
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose MetaARIMA, a pretrained configuration policy based on metalearning that brings transfer learning to classical statistical forecasting at the configuration level rather than the model level. The policy learns from historical experiments which ARIMA configurations achieve top-quantile performance, and recommends promising candidates for new series while preserving interpretability and local estimation.

items.title: How Much Graph Is Too Much? Graph Construction and Exposure in Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We study these choices as graph construction and graph exposure on U.S. state unemployment, traffic speed, and electricity demand. … Late integration alone is insufficient, while adding a fusion gate yields lower mean error in all three tasks.

items.title: PMU Foundation Model Bridge: A Tool for Connecting Synchrophasor Streams to Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper presents PMU Foundation Model Bridge, an open source tool that connects online phasor measurement unit (PMU) or phasor data concentrator (PDC) streams to publicly available time series foundation models (TSFM). … In the initial release, 4 publicly available TSFMs were supported, including Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Timestral, and TimesFM-3.

items.title: Learning What to Share: Expert Specialization for Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: These insights motivate Persistent Closed-Form Routing (PCR), a plug-and-play method that alternates exact conditional estimation of channel-specific mixture weights with gradient-based training of low-rank residual experts around a frozen pretrained forecaster. Averaged over four forecasting horizons, PCR-K4 achieves dataset-balanced mean squared error reductions of 3.86-14.25% relative to the three frozen backbones.

items.title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning
items.summary: From the abstract: We model the cumulative carbon cost of different approaches across a realistic industrial scenario: Chronos-2 amortizes its pretraining cost within months for large or frequently queried deployments, but a classical model remains cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried ones.

items.title: When to Trust Memory: Retrieval-Guided Probabilistic Spatiotemporal Forecasting under Distribution Shift
items.summary: From the abstract: To address this issue, we propose REMIND, a retrieval-guided probabilistic framework for spatiotemporal forecasting under distribution shift.

items.title: DBCM: Dual-Branch Calibration Module for Test-Time Adaptation in Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: Motivated by this observation, we propose the Dual-Branch Calibration Module (DBCM), which shares adaptation capacity across channels through a shared adapter while retaining limited channel-specific flexibility through a low-rank channel-wise adapter, further enhanced by channel mixing and nonlinear gated modulation.

items.title: TempShap: When and How Much a Feature Matters in Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose TempShap, a retrospective, loss-based Shapley framework whose players are the individual input cells $(t,i)$. Its attribution tensor yields temporal-localization and horizon-impact profiles.

items.title: Model-agnostic predictability quantification of multivariable time series
items.summary: From the abstract: In this work, we propose Multivariable Predictability Score (MAPS), a model-agnostic metric for measuring the intrinsic predictability of multivariable time series forecasting tasks.

items.title: Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals: Locally Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We then propose Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals (VCPI), a post-hoc calibration procedure that uses the base forecaster's predictive scale as a baseline, models the volatility of standardized forecast residuals with a Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) model, and applies a multiplicative correction to produce locally adaptive prediction intervals.

items.title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost (DISC), a learnable aggregation framework that uses calibration transfer observations to select, weight, and combine similarity metrics for different downstream tasks.

items.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model
items.summary: From the abstract: We evaluate TimesFM 1, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on 15-minute telemetry from 27 sensor stations across three land-management regimes (Control, Treatment, Scald) at a semi-arid restoration site, forecasting 5 cm and 30 cm soil moisture and enclosure temperature at seven lead times from 1 h to 168 h.

items.title: GateFormer: Forecast-Space Decomposition for Intra-Hour Solar Irradiance Prediction from Sky Images
items.summary: From the abstract: To address this, we introduce GateFormer, a GHI-conditioned dual-decoder ViT for intra-hour global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting through forecast-space decomposition.

items.title: Is spectral predictability enough? Testing Ω-matching for synthetic pretraining under distribution shift
items.summary: From the abstract: We test this hypothesis, which we call predictability-aware pretraining, across three architectures (LSTM, PatchTST, TCN) and three seeds.

items.title: TimeH2O v1 (Hugging Face model page)
items.summary: From the model card: Time series foundation model by H2O.ai. Datasets overlapping with fev-bench, GIFT-Eval, and TIME were excluded from training.

items.title: A Model-Agnostic Correction Framework for Short-Term Building Load Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: Motivated by this idea, we propose WeL-RAC, a model-agnostic Weather-Load Retrieval-Augmented Correction framework that explicitly retrieves such evidence at prediction time. The framework improves the corresponding base forecasters in 90 of 96 dataset-level comparisons.

items.title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: From the abstract: Covariate-aware time series foundation models (TSFMs) accept a future path for a control variable and return a forecast, inviting what-if queries. The query is interventional; the models are trained on observational data.

items.title: Local and Global Recursive Ridge Regression for Online Residual Correction of Frozen Multivariate Forecasters under Label Delay
items.summary: From the abstract: Aiming to combine a small retained state with a large error reduction, we propose DRiC (DCT Ridge Corrector), which fits a ridge regression of the leading discrete cosine transform (DCT) coefficients of the next residual block on those of the frozen forecast and of the latest input block, with sufficient statistics updated recursively.

items.title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To disentangle these effects, we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol with frozen candidate forecasts. Experiments on GIFT-Eval show that AMO improves accuracy, but its gains are bounded by the candidate TSFMs.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning for Short-Term Atmospheric Seeing Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: In this work, we benchmark machine learning models for predicting atmospheric seeing up to two hours in advance, with a particular focus on probabilistic forecasting and uncertainty quantification.

items.title: Rethinking Time Series Tokenization from a Frequency Perspective
items.summary: From the abstract: To overcome this distortion, we propose TimeFT, a nearly distortion-free frequency-based tokenizer for time series data.

items.title: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We investigate this regime for Transformer-based electricity-load forecasting using 3-, 5-, 7-, and 16-state weight quantization across feed-forward-only and attention-plus-feed-forward quantization.

items.title: Asymmetric Bidirectional Predictive Dynamics in Google Search and COVID-19 Time Series: A Multi-Horizon Forecast-Error Analysis
items.summary: From the abstract: We examine eight pre-specified Google Trends-COVID-19 pairs in both directions using matched LightGBM forecasts over rolling 400-day windows and horizons of 1-14 days.

items.title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: From the abstract: We explore two closed-loop forecasting strategies, in which the network's own generated values are fed back into the network as if they were observed past values: (i) model-level and (ii) layer-level closed-loop forecasting.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper compares pretrained inference, full fine-tuning, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) in terms of forecasting accuracy and adaptation efficiency across four electrical load aggregation levels.

items.title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To address this scalability gap, this paper presents a domain-specific foundation-style pretraining framework that learns a shared forecasting model from heterogeneous multi-site and multi-horizon PV data.

items.title: Training-Free Continual Learning for Multimodal Forecasting via Prompt Evolution
items.summary: From the abstract: We argue that continual prompt evolution is a practical, training-free alternative to retraining for multimodal forecasting.

items.title: Dynamic Dual-Feedback Conformal Inference for Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: In this paper, we propose Dynamic Dual-feedback Conformal Inference (DDCI), which incorporates a dual-feedback mechanism consisting of actual feedback and estimated feedback.

items.summary: Abstract opening: Irregular multivariate time series forecasting (IMTSF) requires capturing temporal dynamics and cross-variable dependencies from sparse, asynchronous observations.

items.title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture.

items.title: Paloma: Phase-Conditioned Residual Modulation for Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: Abstract opening: Explicitly modeling periodicity has proven to be an efficient approach for time series forecasting, where the residual, obtained after removing the periodic component from the time series, is typically treated as unstructured noise.

items.title: CVTA: Cross-Variable Temporal Attention for Multivariate Irregular Time Series Prediction
items.summary: From the abstract: In this work, we introduce Cross-Variable Temporal Attention (CVTA), a short-term, continuous-time forecasting framework that learns prediction functions from its compact, interpretable state summarizing recent temporal dynamics across variables.

items.title: Probabilistic Limit Order Book Forecasting with Conditional Diffusion Models
items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce LOBGrad, a conditional DDPM framework for probabilistic LOB forecasting that combines an autoregressive RNN encoder with a diffusion-based generator.

items.title: Multi-site Learning for Forecasting Day-Ahead Wind-Power Production for Onshore Wind Farms in Great Britain with Deep Neural Networks
items.summary: From the abstract: In this study, we train multi-site deep neural networks (DNNs) using pooled historical production and reanalysis weather data from 88 onshore wind Balancing Mechanism Units (BMUs).

items.title: Data-driven forecasting of tropical cloud forest phenology: A dynamical systems and machine learning hybrid approach
items.summary: From the abstract: While traditional phenological models often rely on preconceived functional forms, this study introduces a data-driven hybrid approach that integrates dynamical systems theory with machine learning to forecast flowering and fruiting cycles.

items.title: World Models, Trees and Foundation Models for Retail Forecasting: Evidence from Four Public Data Sets
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper compares models at each grain on four public data sets (M5, six Dominick's categories, Breakfast at the Frat, and Corporación Favorita, the last kept out of all development), over rolling forecast origins with paired tests and model confidence sets. The answer changed with the grain.

items.title: Spectral Adaptive Graph Transformer for Efficient and Scalable Traffic Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce the spectral adaptive graph transformer, whose spatial operator is learned rather than derived from the Laplacian, directed rather than symmetric, and conditioned on the current traffic state rather than a static state, at a cost linear in the number of sensors.

items.title: Compose the Horizon: Parameter-Shared Blockwise Forecasting under a Sequential-Compute Trade-off
items.summary: From the abstract: Recursive Functional Decomposition (RFD) factorizes the horizon mapping into three parameter-shared block predictions.

items.title: Learning volatility-adaptive forgetting via GARCH-modulated LSTM for stock price forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: This paper presents the Gsigmoid-LSTM model, which embeds Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity (GARCH(1,1))-derived volatility estimates into the LSTM forgetting gate through the Gsigmoid activation function, a volatility-adaptive variant of the sigmoid that combines a volatility adjustment factor with slope regulation via a learnable parameter.

items.title: A decomposition-integration framework coupling singular spectrum analysis with a volatility-adaptive LSTM for stock price forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: To address these gaps, this paper proposes CEEMDAN-SE-SSA-VMGL. On five US and Chinese financial series (CSI 300, CSI 500, AAPL, GOOGL, S&P 500), the proposed model is compared with eleven benchmark architectures, lowering the forecasting error by 9% to 24% relative to the best benchmark and by 60% to 70% relative to a standard LSTM.

items.title: Morpheus-2.0: Multiscale Probabilistic Forecasting with Dual-Axis Attention
items.summary: Morpheus-2.0: universal probabilistic forecaster with dual-axis attention.

items.summary: Abstract opening: In time-series forecasting tasks, the use of recursive forecasting on high-dimensional data substantially increases the complexity of the prediction process.

items.title: LagNet: Lag-Structured Operators for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: Abstract opening: Long-term time series forecasting maps a finite history window to an extended future horizon.

items.summary: Abstract opening: Series decomposition has emerged as a widely acknowledged paradigm in deep time series forecasting models.

items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce OrderFlowDiT, a conditional Diffusion Transformer for unnormalized bid and ask volume-at-price fields, trained with an unbalanced optimal-transport (UOT) auxiliary loss.

items.summary: From the abstract: This paper compares methods for estimating current and next-hour speeds on every link from such sparse detectors, using historical probe data for training.

items.title: CGDT-CESN: Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network for Multivariate Time-Series Prediction
items.summary: From the abstract: In this work, a Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network (CGDT-CESN) is proposed, which comprises a modular reservoir architecture with each cluster distinctly specializing in one of the variables in the multivariate time series.

items.title: Learning to Forecast on Multiple Spatiotemporal Hierarchies
items.summary: From the abstract: In this work, we propose a graph deep learning framework that leverages variations across hierarchies as multi-task regularization. We show that jointly learning across these structures can reduce over-specialization to any single hierarchy and improve forecasting performance.

items.title: Learning and Forecasting Multiscale Spatiotemporal Epidemic Dynamics with Lagrangian-Eulerian Graph Neural ODEs
items.summary: From the abstract: We introduce LE-EpiGNODE, which replaces generic message passing with process-specific, mechanism-guided neural operators: age-contact information drives Lagrangian infection generation, whereas mobility drives conservative Eulerian population transport within a structure-preserving universal differential equation.

items.title: ChronoSheaf: Joint Spatio-Temporal Spectral Filtering on Cellular Sheaves
items.summary: From the abstract: Building on this operator, we introduce ChronoSheaf, a spatio-temporal sheaf network with two key components. … We validate ChronoSheaf on a diverse set of spatio-temporal forecasting benchmarks, where it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

items.title: Single-stage joint diffusion of sky images and clear-sky index for ultra-short-term irradiance forecasting: what the frame-to-irradiance stage discards
items.summary: From the abstract: We propose a single-stage alternative that co-denoises the future sky-image and clear-sky-index sequences in one diffusion process, with an irradiance head that reads a denoised preview of the future sky rather than the noised diffusion state.

items.title: Timestral-209M (Hugging Face model page)

items.title: Test-Time Forecasting: Recurrent Depth Enables In-Context Dynamics Prediction
items.summary: Abstract opening: Foundation models for dynamical systems can forecast unseen partial differential equations (PDEs), ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and time series during inference.

items.summary: Abstract opening: Transformers have demonstrated strong performance in long-term time series forecasting (LTSF), yet modeling non-stationary temporal dependencies remains challenging.

items.summary: Abstract opening: Time-series foundation models provide strong zero-shot forecast, but deployment for real-world applications still requires task-specific designs for model inputs and outputs.

items.summary: Abstract opening: Although multivariate time series forecasting has broad application prospects, effectively incorporating exogenous variables remains challenging.

items.title: Quantile-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: We instantiate this approach as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. Across eight benchmarks, Control-TS consistently improves the backbone's CRPS, achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forecasting models, and retains its gains in capacity-matched comparisons.

items.title: VaryST: Generalizable Spatio-Temporal Forecasting Beyond the Closed-World Setting
items.summary: From the abstract: To this end, we propose VaryST, a compact spatio-temporal forecasting model trained from scratch that achieves strong generalization by dynamically constructing predictive context from available long-term observations. … Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets against seventeen baselines show that VaryST achieves strong in-domain forecasting accuracy, substantially improves zero- and few-shot generalization under spatial and temporal changes, and remains robust to varying observation availability.

items.title: Ranked Right, Sized Wrong: Ensemble Spread Fails Silently at Streamflow Extremes
items.summary: From the abstract: Deep learning models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory networks, are increasingly used for operational streamflow forecasting, with ensemble spread providing a signal of predictive uncertainty. As climate change increases the frequency of hydroclimatic extremes, these models will increasingly operate under flow conditions that are rare in their historical records. We therefore evaluate whether ensemble spread remains informative under increasing flows, examining both its magnitude relative to error and its ability to rank errors.

items.title: A two stage statistical framework for cold start spare part demand forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: Accurate demand forecasting for spare parts under true cold-start conditions remains a fundamental challenge due to extreme demand sparsity, zero inflation, and the complete absence of historical demand information. … To address this gap, this study proposes a novel Zero-Inflated Gamma Monte Carlo (ZIG MC) framework that explicitly decomposes demand into occurrence and magnitude components and generates fully probabilistic forecasts suitable for risk-aware inventory decision-making.

items.title: RAID: Semantic Graph Diffusion for True Cold-Start and Cross-Lingual Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: However, true cold-start scenarios, where a new item has no prior observations, violate this assumption. We propose RAID (Retrieval-Augmented Iterative Diffusion) a framework, which replaces history-based correlation learning with metadata-driven semantic retrieval and graph-conditioned diffusion.

items.title: Zero Touch Predictive Orchestration: Automating Time-Series Models for the Cloud-Edge Continuum
items.summary: From the abstract: However, orchestrators face a severe "cold start" problem: newly discovered nodes lack the historical data required to train localized predictive models, while generalized models fail to capture unique hardware and microservice behaviors. To solve this, we propose a fully automated time-series prediction architecture driven by a novel data-mixing methodology.

items.title: Time series Foundation Models based on Physics-Informed Synthetic Histories for Cold-Start Photovoltaic Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: This cold-start setting is addressed with a zero-shot pipeline that generates a synthetic production history from plant metadata and meteorological covariates, enabling time-series foundation models (TSFMs) to forecast through inference-time conditioning.

items.title: CausalPOI: Spatio-Temporal Graph-Based Causal Modeling for Cold-Start POI Check-in Forecasting
items.summary: From the abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel research problem -- cold-start POI check-in forecasting, which aims to predict the future check-in pattern of a newly introduced POI, by modeling its temporal evolution and functional interactions with nearby POIs in a structured urban spatial context.
